title: Sarmatians
fact_summary: Ancient steppe peoples. A 2022 genome study finds Sarmatian ancestry both in Hun-period graves and in the conquering Hungarians.

claims.text: The 2022 study reports “prevalent Sarmatian ancestry in 4 Hun period samples”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: It models the conquerors' core immigrant group as about 50% Mansi and 35% Early or Late Sarmatian ancestry.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: It dates the mixing of the conquerors' ancestors with early Sarmatians to about 643–431 BCE, 53 generations before the conquerors died.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: The ancestors of the conquerors lived in the steppe-forest zone and “admixed with Iranian-speaking early Sarmatians”, probably when the Sarmatians rose to power and drew in neighbouring tribes.
claims.certainty_reason: One study's reading of its own models. The language of the Sarmatians is the authors' characterisation and is not argued on this page.

open_questions.text: The study names its Sarmatian reference genomes only by code. Where were they found, and how well do they stand for all Sarmatians?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
